summary.oneLiner: ONE Sudarshan is the world's leading pigment and color solutions producer, formed by combining Sudarshan Chemical's 75-year pigment legacy with the acquired Heubach Group (including Clariant's former pigments unit), spanning 270+ years of combined expertise.
summary.business: Sudarshan Chemical Industries manufactures and sells organic and inorganic pigments, effect pigments, performance colorants, pearlescent pigments and specialty chemicals used to add color and functional performance to coatings, plastics, printing and digital inks, cosmetics, home and personal care products, and agriculture and other specialty applications. Following the FY2025 acquisition of the Heubach Group's global pigment business, the group serves over 4,000 customers in 120+ countries from 19 manufacturing facilities across 11 countries.

currentContext.strengths: World's leading pigment and color solutions producer per management, with 270+ years of combined expertise across Sudarshan, Heubach and Clariant's former pigments legacies; management describes the company as the most profitable pure-pigment player and third-largest producer globally|Manufacturing footprint of 19 facilities across 11 countries and five continents, giving proximity to customers, supply-chain resilience and agility in responding to regional demand|Broad portfolio of approximately 1,600 products and 63 brands, described as one of the widest ranges in the industry, serving 4,000+ customers across 120+ countries and every major industry|R&D scale of 200+ technology and R&D professionals across global innovation centers, developing sustainable and high-performance pigment solutions co-created with customers|Customer relationships strong enough that several customers recognized the company with 'Best Supplier of the Year' awards during the disruptive integration year
currentContext.strategies: Complete the integration of Sudarshan, Heubach and Clariant's former pigments legacies into 'ONE Sudarshan' with a common culture, operating model and reporting systems|Migrate from four separate SAP environments to one common platform (SAP integration project) to harmonize the system landscape|Pursue value-capture initiatives across growth, cost and cash spanning procurement, operations and support functions to lift the acquired business's profitability|Bring transactional activities back to India through a newly inaugurated Global Capability Center (GCC) in Pune to streamline operations|Prioritize customer service, supply reliability, and commercial/technical support to rebuild trust with customers of the acquired business, deliberately not chasing inventory reduction in the first six to nine months post-acquisition|Leverage the expanded global manufacturing footprint (19 facilities, 11 countries, five continents) through strategic realignment of production for local proximity to customers and supply-chain resilience|Lead in sustainable and regulatory-compliant color technology: zinc-free anticorrosive pigments, compostable/biodegradable-plastics-compliant colorants, NIR-detectable blacks for automated recycling, and biocide-free/preservative-free colorant formulations|Reactivate the CICP (Complex Inorganic Colored Pigments) innovation pipeline by combining Sudarshan and Heubach expertise|Act as a solutions provider for evolving regulatory requirements, e.g. offering compliant Red 2 pigment combinations to replace chemistries like PR 53:1|For FY2025-26 the Board recommended a Final Dividend of Rs.5.00 per equity share of Rs.2.00 each (250%), for declaration by shareholders at the 75th AGM. On CSR, the Company commits to spend at least 2% of the average net profits of the three immediately preceding financial years, per Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, focused on women empowerment, environment, health, community development and education. No amounts were transferred to General Reserve for FY26, and the Company has not accepted public deposits. No broader dividend-policy philosophy statement is present in this excerpt.
currentContext.expansion: During FY2025-26 the Company continued its expansion plans, incurring capex spend primarily aimed at augmenting production capacities at its Roha and Mahad (Maharashtra) facilities. Separately, on the group's inorganic growth: Sudarshan Europe B.V. (wholly-owned subsidiary) completed the acquisition of the Global Pigment Business Operations of the Heubach Group on 3rd March 2025 (agreement signed 11th October 2024), comprising Heubach's German entities and a Luxembourg holding company with India and USA investments. Following this, a mandatory SEBI open-offer for Sudarshan Colorants India Limited (formerly Heubach Colorants India Limited) was completed in October 2025, after which the Company indirectly holds 70.25% of that target company through the Acquirer and persons-acting-in-concert entities. On the operational-integration side, 'Project Integra' is consolidating four legacy SAP systems into a single unified landscape to give real-time visibility into global inventory and capacity; a Global Capability Center (GCC) was inaugurated in Pune as a centralized operations hub. Management's stated future priorities for manufacturing are process optimization and automation, disciplined capacity utilization across the 19 global sites, and continued investment in facility upgrades, quality systems and safety standards.
currentContext.mdna: Management expects the demand normalization observed from Q4 FY26 in the acquired (Heubach) business to continue|Second and third quarters of FY26 were impacted by global customers working down inventories (destocking) in the acquired business, which weighed on revenue in those quarters|Revenue in the legacy Sudarshan business remained broadly flat/stable, attributed to a deliberate rationalization of the go-to-market and distributor model in parts of Europe and Latin America, described as a temporary blip|Focused value-capture initiatives delivered a positive EBITDA turnaround for the acquired business as the year progressed|The expanded global manufacturing footprint is described as a structural advantage giving proximity to customers, supply-chain resilience, and agility to respond to regional demand|Company describes itself as not immune to demand shifts and policy volatility, but says its ability to serve customers has never been stronger given its expanded global presence

risks.risk: Complexity of integrating three pigment legacies (Sudarshan, Heubach and Clariant's former pigments business) into 'ONE Sudarshan'
risks.note: Integration spans commercial, operational, technology and support workstreams, including migrating from four separate SAP environments to one common platform and aligning teams around a common operating model; execution risk during a multi-year integration.

risks.risk: Demand volatility and customer destocking in the acquired (Heubach) business
risks.note: The acquired business experienced customer destocking during parts of FY26, which management says impacted revenue, particularly in the second and third quarters.

risks.risk: Disruption from go-to-market and distributor model changes
risks.note: Revenue in the legacy Sudarshan business was influenced by changes to the go-to-market and distributor model in parts of Europe and Latin America during the year.

risks.risk: Broad geographic and multi-source risk exposure
risks.note: Company operates across diverse geographies and states this exposes it to a broad spectrum of risks -- industry-specific challenges, sustainability concerns, operational disruptions and financial exposures -- monitored via its Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework.
Explicitly identified by the company as one of the risk sources monitored and mitigated under its ERM framework.

Net debt stood at Rs.755 crores as at 31st March 2026, with a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.3x, reflecting debt taken on (alongside equity) to fund the Heubach Group acquisition; balance-sheet focus and working-capital efficiency are stated as ongoing management priorities.

thesis: Sudarshan is consolidating the global color-pigment industry: a year after acquiring the Heubach business (which itself included the never-fully-integrated Clariant pigments + Heubach legacy), it is now the #2 pigment player globally with 19 sites in 11 countries, 4,000+ customers, 1,600+ products. The structural edge is that >50% of manufacturing assets sit in low-cost Asia vs <1% for competitors. The investment case is a 3-stage turnaround: (1) stabilize the acquired/insolvent business (done — positive EBITDA delivered), (2) extract synergies + value capture to lift acquired EBITDA toward EUR 90-100mn over 3-4 years, (3) deleverage the acquisition finance via ballooning repayment funded by that EBITDA. Q4FY26 was the proof-point: strong volume rebound as insolvency-era destocking ended and customer trust was rebuilt.
scorecard (q4fy26): Note: PAT not separately disclosed in transcript; YoY consol comparison is not meaningful (only ~1 month of acquired-group consolidation in the prior-year base).
guidance (critical): FY27 acquired-group EBITDA: EUR 35 mn (explicit). Built on value-capture + integration benefits + "very moderate" growth given geopolitics.

Medium-term acquired-group EBITDA: EUR 90-100 mn over the next 3-4 years (reaffirmed from acquisition-time guidance). Drivers: synergies, value-capture initiatives, sales growth. Crucially — requires NO capex for volume; existing capacity + debottlenecking suffices.
Legacy Sudarshan growth FY27: 8-10% (despite geopolitical crisis).
Legacy Sudarshan margin: maintain healthy >14% business-EBITDA margin into FY27 by passing on cost increases.
Inventory: further reduce EUR 15-20 mn in FY27 (gradually) → reaches "normal state," at which point reported EBITDA and business EBITDA will converge/merge.
Industry baseline: global pigment industry grows ~3-4% (tracks regional GDP). Q4 growth was company-specific (winning back business + destocking ending), NOT industry growth.
Tax: acquired-group ETR currently elevated (conservatively did not recognize deferred taxes in a few entities); assume similar range for the year.
Debt repayment: acquisition finance has a BALLOONING schedule — first repayment starts in FY27 and steps up; funded by EBITDA trajectory.
order book / pipeline: No pigment "order book" (flow business). RIECO is project-based: FY26 growth came from execution of high-value projects; transformation "not over," numbers expected to keep improving over coming years.
segment: Pigments (Legacy India): flattish FY26 rev (distributor rationalization in EU/LatAm); >14% business-EBITDA margin; 8-10% growth guided FY27.
Pigments (Acquired = Heubach+Clariant): Q4 EUR 61mn rev run-rate (+33% QoQ), EUR 11mn business EBITDA; strongest in coatings; broad-based recovery across all segments/regions; pure volume-led.
RIECO: INR 268cr FY26 rev (+17.5%), EBITDA turned positive INR 10cr (from −17cr). Previously floated for potential hive-off; now being turned around first.
growth / optionality: Synergy/value-capture engine: entire integration benefit to flow over next TWO financial years; value-capture is the main driver behind FY27 EUR 35mn and the EUR 90-100mn medium-term target.
One SAP "Project Integra": consolidating 4 ERP systems + 180 peripheral apps into 1 — targeted complete by FY-end (this year). Big efficiency lever.
GCC (Global Capability Centre) in India: bringing transaction processes back to India for cost efficiency; fully operational in 6-8 months.
Frankfurt → specialty centre; commodity → India: already moved some commodity products from Frankfurt to the Roha (India) Heubach site; Frankfurt stays specialty.
Non-core asset disposal: explicitly flagged as "definitely an opportunity" — exploring divestment of non-core/non-strategic acquired assets/plants; thought process still early, to revisit.
Capacity: enough headroom in both legacy + acquired plants (plus debottlenecking) to deliver the 3-4yr targets without growth capex.
margins & cost: Business EBITDA introduced to strip out inventory-destocking noise (overhead absorption B/S↔P&L). Once inventory normalizes (after EUR 15-20mn more reduction), reported = business EBITDA.
Acquired GM 4-5 ppt above legacy; offset by higher acquired fixed costs.

Cost headwinds: petroleum-derived RM price + supply constraints; energy now 6-7% of revenue (Europe-heavy); higher logistics costs AND higher logistics returns. Mitigation: region-specific price pass-through (some lag by region/competitor country-of-origin), global footprint as supply hedge, accelerated value capture, cross-functional war-room team.
Mgmt explicitly will NOT profiteer from chemical-price inflation on old inventory — passing through only actual cost increases to preserve volumes & customer trust.
capex: No growth capex required for the EUR 90-100mn EBITDA path — existing capacity + debottlenecking suffice. India expansion completed earlier; FY27 is the last year of the prior 3-4yr ramp window but headroom remains.
capital allocation: Deleveraging is priority: net debt INR 934cr (Dec-25) → INR 755cr (Mar-26); net-debt/equity 0.3x.
Cash sits largely in Indian entity; debt largely in acquired entities — acquired debt to be serviced from acquired-group cash flow generation. Ballooning repayment of acquisition finance starts FY27.
Potential non-core asset sales as a future deleveraging/value lever.
Governance: family stepped down from Board & management; management professionalized; family chose to "de-promoterize" (move to non-promoter) while remaining committed to growth.
risks: Geopolitics (Middle East/Gulf war): RM price + supply constraints, energy inflation, logistics disruption; near-term demand "muted" as customers stay cautious and avoid high-cost inventory build.
Pass-through lag: region/competitor-dependent timing risk on recovering cost inflation.
Debt structure mismatch: cash in India, debt in acquired entities; ballooning repayment ramps up.
Execution: triple-integration (Heubach + Clariant + never-completed prior merger), One-SAP cutover risk, harmonizing reporting/leadership gaps.
RIECO: turnaround incomplete, numbers not yet at expectation.
management tone: Confident and detailed, leaning into a credible turnaround narrative ("very robust Q4," beat own EBITDA & inventory-reduction targets, net debt down INR 179cr QoQ). Candid about challenges — openly described silo mentality, broken supply chains, legacy mindset, poor customer service inherited. Disciplined messaging on not profiteering and protecting volumes/trust. Cautious specifically on near-term demand due to geopolitics ("temporary blip"), but reaffirmed all medium-term targets. Net: bullish on structure, realistic on near-term.
non-obvious insights: Q4 strength is NOT restocking — mgmt insistent it's genuine buyback after destocking ended; no price hikes taken in Q4, so the +33% QoQ is pure volume + value-capture leverage (other opex up only ~13% vs sales up 33% → strong operating leverage).

Two big accounting distortions to model around: +INR 37cr non-cash PPA credit and −INR 82cr inventorized-overhead release both sit inside the INR 73cr reported EBITDA; and Q4 depreciation of INR 50cr is artificially low (use INR 347cr/yr).
EUR 35mn FY27 acquired EBITDA already bakes in only "very moderate" growth — i.e., conservative; upside if geopolitics eases.
The EUR 90-100mn target needs zero growth capex — it's a pure margin/synergy story, which de-risks capital intensity.
Insolvency surcharge rolled back — they removed the insolvency-era surcharge customers resented, pressuring near-term profitability but rebuilding trust (won "Best Supplier of the Year" awards).
De-promoterization of family members is a structural governance shift, not a distress signal.
challenges → beneficiaries: (Most challenges here are company-specific turnaround/macro items rather than cross-stock value-chain shifts; table kept minimal.)
qoq log: Q4FY26 (this call): Business EBITDA INR 118cr (acquired EUR 11mn, beat EUR 9-10mn guide); reported EBITDA INR 73cr (distorted by +37cr PPA credit & −82cr overhead release). Net debt INR 755cr (from 934cr in Dec-25), ND/E 0.3x. Inventory cut EUR 29mn (vs 20mn plan). Acquired rev run-rate EUR 61mn (+33% QoQ). RIECO FY26 rev INR 268cr / EBITDA +10cr (turnaround). FY27 guide: acquired EBITDA EUR 35mn, legacy growth 8-10%, further EUR 15-20mn inventory cut. Medium-term: EUR 90-100mn acquired EBITDA in 3-4yrs, no growth capex. Geopolitics = near-term demand muted.

Q3FY26 (prior, referenced): Acquired rev run-rate EUR 47mn (weak; Dec seasonally muted). Net debt INR 934cr (Dec-25). Business-EBITDA concept first introduced. Guided to liquidate ~EUR 35-40mn inventory over 2-3 qtrs.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

hero.oneLiner: ONE Sudarshan is the world's leading pigment and color solutions producer, formed by combining Sudarshan Chemical's 75-year pigment legacy with the acquired Heubach Group (including Clariant's former pigments unit), spanning 270+ years of combined expertise.
